# Shared register operations

Manage `<product>/.po/register.jsonl` according to `schemas/register.schema.json`: append-only JSON Lines for assumptions, questions, blockers, and decisions. It is the same taxonomy as ai-sdlc-loop's shared surface register, plus the optional aidev-po extension (DEC-002 in `docs/decisions.md`), so the register can go to ai-sdlc-loop in the gate bundle and come back.

## When to use

Every producer, reviewer, `evidence-auditor`, `challenger`, and `po` when recording, reading, or resolving register items.

## Register rules (`schemas/register.schema.json`)

- File path inside the product folder: `<products-repo>/<slug>/.po/register.jsonl`.
- Append-only JSONL: never edit or delete existing lines; state changes are `update` lines referencing `ref`.
- The stage goes in the shared `phase` field (there is no `stage` field): `idea`, `audience`, `actors`, `systems`, `scope`, `workshops`, `presentations`, `fsd`. Lines merged back from ai-sdlc-loop carry its phase names (`Plan`, `Design`, ... or `all`); they are valid too.
- Valid `type` values: `assumption`, `question`, `blocker` (shared with ai-sdlc-loop), and `decision` (aidev-po extension). A `blocker` stops the stage, or stops it being done correctly, until resolved. The learning loop adds `feedback` and `attribution` (extension), which only `po` writes, with `register.py add --record <FB-n|AT-n>` (skill `feedback-intake`, command `/po-feedback`); they never appear in a register-request block.
- Valid `status` values: `open`, `surfaced`, `answered`, `dismissed`, `duplicate` (shared), `decided`, `superseded` (extension).
- Valid `by` values on updates: `coordinator`, `human` (the user is the `human`).
- Optional declare fields from the extension: `item_ids` (array of item IDs) and `record` (the `FB-`/`AT-` id, required for feedback and attribution).

## Register-request block format

Every agent output (and reviewer/auditor/challenger report) ends with `## Assumptions and open questions` containing verbatim:

```text
=== REGISTER REQUESTS ===
[ASSUMPTION: <one-line statement>]
[QUESTION: <one-line statement (include recommended answer)>]
[BLOCKER: <one-line statement>]
[DECISION: <one-line statement>]
=== END REGISTER REQUESTS ===
```

Write `None.` alone between the delimiters if there are no entries.

## Producer: dos and don'ts

Do:
- End every output and report with `## Assumptions and open questions` and a valid `=== REGISTER REQUESTS ===` block
- Include a recommended answer in every `[QUESTION: ...]` statement
- Use `python3 scripts/register.py` (when shell access is available) or let `po` ingest the block verbatim via `python3 scripts/register.py ingest - --register <path> --agent <name> --phase <stage> --via coordinator`
- Use `[BLOCKER: ...]` only for something that stops the stage, or stops it being done correctly, until resolved; anything else that needs an answer is a `[QUESTION: ...]`
- Curate before each gate (`po`): mark duplicates (`duplicate`), evidence-settled items (`dismissed`), rate `impact`/`urgency`, surface to user (`surfaced`), and record answers/decisions (`answered`, `decided`, `superseded`)
- After an ai-sdlc-loop run on the gate bundle, merge its register copy back with `python3 scripts/register.py merge --from <bundle>/register.jsonl --register <path>` (appends only lines the product register lacks; writes nothing if any line fails)

Don't:
- Write a `stage` field or `by: "user"` (written before DEC-002; `python3 scripts/register.py migrate --write --register <path>` fixes an old register)
- Edit or delete lines in `.po/register.jsonl`
- Reword, merge, reorder, or drop lines when `po` ingests an agent's register-request block
- Leave `=== REGISTER REQUESTS ===` out of an output or findings file

## Steps

1. Agent finishes artefact/findings and appends `## Assumptions and open questions` with `=== REGISTER REQUESTS ===`.
2. `po` ingests the block verbatim into `<product>/.po/register.jsonl` (if the agent did not run `scripts/register.py ingest` itself).
3. `po` runs `python3 scripts/register.py list --open --register <path>` and curates duplicates/ratings.
4. At the gate, `po` updates surfaced items (`surfaced`), records user choices (`answered`/`decided`), and validates with `python3 scripts/register.py check --register <path>`.

## Self-check

- [ ] Does the output end with `## Assumptions and open questions` and a syntactically valid `=== REGISTER REQUESTS ===` block?
- [ ] Are all `[QUESTION: ...]` lines paired with a recommended answer?
- [ ] Does `python3 scripts/register.py check --register <path>` pass with zero errors?

## Adversarial reviewer

- Fail (`P1`) any producer or cross-cutting output missing `## Assumptions and open questions` or a valid `=== REGISTER REQUESTS ===` block.
- Fail (`P1`) any register entry using an invalid type, a `stage` field instead of `phase`, a `phase` that is not the stage it was written in, or mutated/deleted historical JSONL lines.
- Check that no open blocker and no open high-impact/high-urgency question was silently ignored before advancing a stage.
